Modules and the Full Coverage Matrix

import ↔ @import

psa imports are supported for the program's own modules: the driver merges import / from ... import across the program's .psa files, and an import json with no same-named local file binds the psa_std library module instead (census, batch D6; a from-import of a standard-library module is loudly refused in v1). SLA's @import is a compile-time merge of the named file — the standard library ("sa_std/...") and the program's own .sla files use the same form, as every program in this section shows for the standard library. The pair below is two files on each side.

psaSLA
# mathx.psa
def triple(x):
    return x * 3

# main.psa
from mathx import triple

print(triple(14))  # 42
 
// helper.sla
fn triple(x: i32) -> i32 {
    return x * 3;
}

// main.sla
@import "sa_std/io/print.sai"
@import "sa_std/fmt.sai"
@import "helper.sla"

fn main() -> i32 {
    println("{}", triple(14));
    return 0;
}

Verified output (SLA): 42, exit code 0.

The Full Matrix

Every basic syntax point in this section, with the psa-side status from the syntax census (2026-11-25, updated 2026-11-26; task-171 items noted where they supersede the census) and the SLA counterpart. "Supported" on the psa side means the census marks the construct implemented and end-to-end verified; the SLA column names the form used — and compile-verified — in this section.

Syntax pointpsa statusSLA counterpart
CommentsSupported (#)// only; no block comment (parser-verified)
Variables and typesSupported (dynamic binding, no annotation)let (mutable by default), const, static types
Numbers and arithmeticSupported (+ - * / // % **)+ - * / %; integer / = psa //; no **
StringsSupported (dynamic string values)Literals; len, str_eq
f-stringsPartial — basic interpolation; format specs/conversions implemented as task 171-A, pending integration; float interpolation blocked by (xxiii)No f-string; println/format placeholders
Booleans and logicSupported (and/or/not)&&/||/! on bool
if/elif/elseSupportedif / else if / else with blocks
Ternary expressionSupported (x if c else y)If-expression if c { x } else { y }
whileSupported (while/else is a gap)while with break/continue
for / rangePartial — range in the for header and over lists/strings; range as a value is a gapfor i in a..b; index loops over len
Function definitions and returnSupported (defaults, keyword args, *args/**kwargs; annotations not supported)fn, fully typed, no defaults
ListsPartial — literals, indexing, assignment, append supported; a container literal as a call argument is refusedVec<T>: push, indexing, len
DictsSupported (dynamic, insertion-ordered)HashMap: insert, get → Option
TuplesSupported (literal + unpacking)(T, U), .0/.1, let (a, b); (i32, i32) literals hit a registered projection defect — use (i64, i64)
SetsSupported (literals; method set per census batch D5)HashSet: insert, contains, len
Indexing and slicingSupported (incl. negative indices and full slicing)Indexing yes; no negative indices, no slice syntax — explicit copy loop
printSupported (multi-argument; float arguments blocked by (xxiii), fix landed, confirmation pending)println with {} placeholders
importSupported (own modules merged; import binds psa_std when no local file; stdlib from-import refused in v1)@import compile-time merge for std and own files alike
Classes and methodsSupported (single inheritance; super()/multiple inheritance refused)struct + impl; new by convention
ExceptionsSupported (try/except/finally, raise; runtime panics uncatchable)No try form: Result<T, E> for recoverable, panic(code) for unrecoverable
NoneSupported (a real dynamic value)No null; Option<T> + match
ComprehensionsSupported (list/dict/set + generator expressions)No comprehension syntax; explicit loop + push

Recorded psa Gaps With No Page of Their Own

  • Walrus operator := — front-end gap (census).
  • Byte strings b"" and raw strings r"" — front-end gap (census).
  • is / is not — gap at census time (no identity semantics in v1); implemented as task 171-B (identity = tag + payload equality), pending integration.
  • Arbitrary-precision integers — gap: psa integers are i64 and overflow fails loudly; a bigint substrate item has since landed in the SLA standard library (S4) but is not wired into psa integers.
  • while/else and for/else — front-end gap (census).

Key Points of This Section

  • psa and SLA meet at the statement level: nearly every basic Python construct has a direct SLA form, and this section shows each pair as a complete, runnable program.
  • The real differences are systematic, not incidental: dynamic vs static typing, exceptions vs Result/panic, None vs Option, and psa-only sugar (slicing, comprehensions, f-strings) vs explicit SLA loops and placeholder formatting.
  • Every SLA program here was compiled and run on the stated toolchain before being written down; every psa limitation named here traces to the syntax census or a numbered task (171-A, 171-B), not to impression.
